tts_summary:
Here's your midday market update for Tuesday, September 22nd.

The broad market is going nowhere fast. The S&P 500 is essentially flat, the equal-weight S&P is down 10 basis points, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is climbing 30 basis points, and the Dow is lagging down 43 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent crude is hovering near $100, off fractionally, with some diplomatic hope around Iran — reports suggest Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ease military pressure. Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline also appears to be coming back online at least partially, which is keeping oil in check.

The bigger story for trading right now is what's coming over the next ten days in AI. Investors are positioning ahead of Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night at 7pm Eastern, followed by OpenAI's developer day on September 29th, and then Micron earnings on September 30th. That cluster of catalysts is driving outperformance in semiconductor and AI-linked names — you're seeing strength in names like Arm, ASML, Google, Meta, Micron, Marvel, and Oracle today.

On the earnings front, AutoZone beat on fiscal Q4 earnings per share — $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03 — but the quality is questionable. About 145 basis points of gross margin help came from tariff refunds and another 105 basis points from a non-cash accounting item. Domestic comps missed at plus 1.6 versus the expected plus 3.1. Management said linearity was positive in the quarter, which is keeping the stock afloat, but this wasn't a clean beat. MillerKnoll was a cleaner story — fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents crushed the Street's 36 cent estimate, and even stripping out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still beat at 42 cents. THOR Industries was the disappointment — fiscal Q4 EPS of 78 cents missed the 87-cent estimate, gross margins fell 230 basis points year over year to 12.4 percent, and management flagged a difficult macro environment.

On the company news side, Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads and Shopify has agreed to allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform — a notable contrast to Amazon, which blocked Muse. That dynamic is clearly helping Meta's setup into Wednesday's keynote. Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial data on its GLP-1 drug showing 22 percent weight loss, a strong result in a competitive space. Cognex is acquiring depth-sensing camera company RealSense for roughly $500 million upfront to build out its physical AI and robotics capabilities. And Quest Diagnostics and LabCorp are both getting hit hard today after CMS released Medicare lab service payment rates with a larger-than-expected cut.

Financials are broadly the worst performers — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers all underperforming. Managed care is also weak. Aerospace and defense is lagging alongside autos.

Bottom line: the market is in a wait-and-see mode on Iran and geopolitics, while AI bulls are loading up ahead of a critical stretch of catalysts. Tonight watch for KBH and WOR after the close, and Wednesday's main event is that Zuckerberg keynote. Stay focused on how Meta and the AI complex trade into and out of that event.
